  WHY: The selector can resume a session that is instructed to act before or during the reset period.

  WHY: The explicitly negated wait can be classified as a limit wait and the session resumed despite the instruction not to wait.

  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash]
  PROBLEM: The fallback classifies text beginning with a wait/limit prefix as a limit wait when it contains a limit word and a wait word, even when a later retry instruction is actionable.
  WHY: “Wait for the limit. Please retry the request.” can bypass the unanswered-request check and trigger an automatic resume.

  WHY: The pickup can create a resume trigger that executes the session before a human answers, defeating the ask-first gate.

- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/usage_limit_resumes.py:line 348 | severity=blocker | confidence=[5]

  PROBLEM: The test expects “Usage limit reached. Retry the request, not waiting until the reset.” to return false, but the implementation returns true.
  WHY: The test and implementation disagree on the classifier result, so either the test is failing or the reported passing test count is inaccurate.
- docs/implement-plan/issue-6102-skip-unanswered-question-resumes.md:lines 7-10 and 17 | severity=major | confidence=[5]

  WHY: `implement-plan-claude` treats `Status: BLOCKED` as a stop, so the stale status can prevent the project from advancing.
- docs/plans/issue-6102-skip-unanswered-question-resumes-plan.md:line 76 | severity=nit | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The implementation step says to “add the four patterns,” although the selector defines seven regex pattern constants plus `LIMIT_WAIT_VOCABULARY`.
  WHY: The plan gives future implementers an inaccurate inventory of the classifier changes.
